topic: Patents and prior art, verified against the patent pages (preliminary scan, not legal advice, not a freedom-to-operate opinion)
summary: PRELIMINARY SCAN ONLY: not legal advice, not a freedom-to-operate opinion, not a patentability opinion. Run 2026-11-12. Google Patents refuses curl and WebFetch (HTTP 503) from this network, but pages and the search endpoint worked from a real Chrome tab, so every row in the table below was read from its Google Patents page (claim 1, assignee, dates, machine-derived status); EP 4019251 B1 was also read from the EPO publication server. Compared with the earlier agent (agents/spec-ip-landscape.json), which worked from the USPTO search only: (a) the three Harvard / MIT-Harvard applications it left as 'grant not determined' are all Abandoned; (b) the three building-scale wood-bilayer families whose claims it could not read are now read, and all three are narrow: ETH/Empa WO2018033422 claims a lever-coupled shading device and is Ceased; Stuttgart EP4019251 B1 (granted 2026-03-25, opposition window still open) and the Empa/ETH/Stuttgart German national phase DE112019001411 claim pre-conditioning layers at one humidity so the glued part self-shapes at a target climate; none covers a printed resin or powder element; (c) the granted MIT/Stratasys US 11155025 B2 claim 1 is narrower than the earlier summary implied (two joints in series, a planar member, members that touch to limit curvature) but it is the live patent nearest a resin-printed differential-swelling part and runs to about 2034-02-25. CROWDED: printed stimulus-responsive objects in general (MIT/Stratasys), hygromorphic coatings and composites (MIT, NTU, USAF), hydrogel 4D printing (Harvard, now abandoned, UT, CityU, Accenture), wood bilayer building parts (ETH, Empa, Stuttgart), and, as prior ART rather than live rights, the bilayer mechanics themselves: the ETH specification already cites Timoshenko 1925, states that an optimum thickness ratio exists (0.2-0.3 for wood) and reports measured curvature changes. OPEN, by keyword: zero Google Patents documents combine a theorem prover or proof assistant with material, geometry or additive-manufacturing design (queries listed in the table); the nearest are a 2010 Microsoft design-space exploration patent (expired, software architectures) and a 2020 PARC satisfiability-solver manufacturing planner (live, integrated circuits), plus a granted Toyota computational design method for shape-morphing structures (live), which shows that design-method claims in this field are grantable. WHAT THE TEAM COULD PLAUSIBLY CLAIM, if it files before public disclosure (counsel to confirm grace-period rules): (1) a design-and-verification METHOD in which candidate geometries or layups are released to a printer only with a machine-checked proof that they satisfy stated laws (most open, but must show a concrete technical effect); (2) a certified FILE FORMAT binding geometry, material assignment and a proof (open, but data-structure claims face eligibility objections); (3) a specific GEOMETRY found by the constrained search with a measured, unexpected response (narrow); (4) a COMPOSITION (least likely, since stock Formlabs resins are the vendor's formulations and hygromorphic compositions are heavily claimed). 'License your patent' presupposes a patent the team may not hold: no filing by the team was searched for by name or found. Limits: Google's status labels are machine-derived and not authoritative; no Espacenet, Patentscope, CNIPA, JPO or CPC-class search was possible; Formlabs's own patents were not searched; absence of keyword hits is not proof of absence.
lay_summary: This is a first look, not legal advice, at who already owns ideas close to ours. Plenty of people have patented things that bend or curl when they get wet or when the air gets damp, including MIT, Harvard, two Swiss universities and Stuttgart, so we cannot claim 'a plate that curls in humidity' as ours. Several of the best-known older filings have already lapsed or been dropped, which makes them public knowledge anyone may use rather than fences. What we did not find anywhere is a patent that uses a computer-checked proof to decide which shapes are allowed to be printed, a bit like a spell-checker that refuses to print a design unless the maths is signed off. If the team files on that method before showing it publicly, that is where something ownable might sit; the team does not yet hold such a patent, so there is nothing to license today. A patent lawyer must check all of this before anyone relies on it.

glossary.plain: A quick keyword look at patent records, not the thorough professional search a lawyer would order.
A lawyer's formal opinion on whether making or selling something would infringe someone else's live patent; this report is not one.
The set of filings in different countries that all stem from one first application.
The first and usually broadest sentence in a patent that says exactly what is protected.
The earliest filing date, used to decide who was first.
Anything made public before a filing date, including old patents and papers, which can block a later patent.
Labels meaning the owner no longer holds an enforceable right; Google's labels are automatic and can be wrong.
Changing shape when the humidity changes.
Two glued layers that swell by different amounts, so the pair curls like a bimetal strip.
3D printing something designed to change shape later, time being the fourth dimension.
Software that checks a mathematical proof step by step so no gap can slip through.
A cheap early patent filing that fixes a date while the full application is prepared.
A fixed period after a European patent is granted in which anyone may ask the patent office to revoke it.
Two kinds of 3D printing: SLA hardens liquid resin with light, SLS fuses plastic powder with a laser.

findings.claim: The ETH/Empa specification states Timoshenko's 1925 result as prior knowledge: for each stiffness ratio an optimum thickness ratio exists, and for wood it is 0.2-0.3. The thickness-ratio optimum of a hygro-bilayer is therefore published, patent-document prior art (it is an optimum, not the 3/2 ceiling).
findings.evidence_quote: For each stiffness ratio, there exists an optimum thickness ratio to achieve the same maximum bending (Timoshenko, Analysis of Bimetal thermostat, 1925).

findings.claim: The same specification reports measured curvature changes for beech 4 mm + spruce 0.8 mm bilayers going from 85% to 35% RH in 24 h: 0.00818 mm^-1 (plain beech), 0.00971 (horizontal strips), 0.01011 (diagonal strips).
findings.evidence_quote: The homogenous (the sample were the beech was not milled) had a MC loss of 31 % and a change of curvature of 0.00818 mm"1.

findings.claim: Own calculation using the project-record ceiling kappa*h/d_eps <= 3/2: the plain beech/spruce bilayer (h=4.8 mm, dkappa=0.00818 mm^-1) needs a differential free strain of at least 0.00818*4.8/1.5 = 0.0262 (2.6%); strips give 3.1% and 3.2%. This is consistent with the patent's stated layer difference of at least 3%, and f(m=0.2,n=25)=1.5 shows the patent's 0.2-0.3 thickness ratio sits at the ceiling when the modulus ratio is about 25 (m^2 n = 1); that modulus ratio is not stated in the patent and I did not verify it.

University of Stuttgart EP 4019251 B1 is granted (mention of grant 2026-03-25), Active, with only an EP family listed; claim 1 is a method that obtains target climate data (RH2, T2), selects layer type/orientation/thickness, pre-conditions at a different RH1/T1, bonds, and relies on the part changing to a final shape in the target climate. Opposition may be filed within nine months of the grant mention, i.e. to about 2026-12-25 (my arithmetic).

findings.claim: Keyword searches on Google Patents found no document combining a theorem prover or proof assistant with material, geometry or additive-manufacturing design: 'theorem prover' AND 'additive manufacturing' returned 1 result (an unrelated robotics network); 'proof assistant' material design returned 22 with the top 10 unrelated; 'formal verification' AND 'additive manufacturing' geometry returned 3, unrelated. Negative keyword result only.

Literature check: arXiv API totalResults is 0 for 'theorem prover' AND 'material design', 'proof assistant' AND 'additive manufacturing', 'Lean 4' AND 'metamaterial', and 'proof assistant' AND '4D printing'; Crossref queries returned only software/hardware verification and generic additive-manufacturing standards. The closest published work is Lean formalisation of chemical physics (Bobbin 2024), not a design gate.

Hygromorphic building-element research is very active and public: a 2025 paper on rice-husk 4D-printed hygromorphic building skin and a 2026 chapter on a simulation framework for porosity-driven hygromorphic bilayers both resolve in Crossref, as does the 2024 Nature Communications weather-responsive 4D-printed shading paper. These are prior art against broad claims on printed hygromorphic facade elements.

Google Patents returned zero documents for hygroscopic 'shape-changing' facade panel 3D printed, and only five for 'hygromorphic' AND '3D printing' (MIT US9931829, CMU US20220322599, Accenture EP3988317, Purdue US20260001811, IIT EP4783825): printed hygromorphic building elements are thinly patented by keyword, with the heavy prior art in papers.

key_claims.claim: The live patent nearest a resin-printed differential-swelling part is MIT/Stratasys US 11155025 B2 (Active, to about 2034-02-25), but its claim 1 is narrow (two joints in series with planar and curvature-limiting members); the broad parent application is Abandoned.

key_claims.claim: Zero Google Patents documents and zero arXiv records combine a theorem prover / proof assistant with material, geometry or additive-manufacturing design; the nearest are an expired Microsoft design-space-exploration patent, a live PARC solver-based manufacturing planner for ICs, and a live Toyota computational design method for inflatable shape-morphing structures. A design-and-verification method is therefore the most plausible ownable subject matter, subject to counsel.

recommendations: Ask a patent attorney about a provisional filing BEFORE the paper, repo or live dashboard publicly discloses the law-constrained design pipeline; public disclosure can be prior art against later filings in most jurisdictions (grace-period rules differ; counsel to confirm).

Frame any claim as a design-and-verification method with a concrete technical effect (for example a slicer or printer that refuses to build without a valid machine-checked certificate, or a measured property guaranteed by the certified bound), not as a humidity bilayer. A certified file format needs a technical-effect hook to survive eligibility objections.

Do not describe the proof of concept as a 'new material composition' if it uses stock Formlabs resins or powders; a specific verified geometry with a measured, unexpected response is the more defensible physical claim.

Before pitching a printed hygromorphic facade element to Mamou-Mani, order a professional search of CPC classes B33Y, B29C64, E04F10, E06B9, G06F30 and G06N5 with Espacenet and CNIPA, and watch EP 4019251 B1 (opposition window to about 2026-12-25) and MIT/Stratasys US 11155025 B2 (to about 2034-02-25).
